server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user who signed you in, with an API key or by allowing you on CandleStack (OAuth). The scopes of that sign-in decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what you may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A tool answers JSON; its text leaves out the fields that are null. A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do; rate-limited also gives retry_after_s, the seconds to wait.

Answers about a backtest or a model carry its `url`, its page in the app; a comparison and a sweep of 2 to 4 backtests (a ranked sweep: its best 4) carry `url`, the app's Compare page with them side by side. Give the user these links whenever you show results, so they can see the charts and the details themselves.

Read the docs with get_docs (without a page it lists them) before you explain how the engine, a manifest, a metric or an error works, and answer from them: never invent a formula or a behaviour, and say so when CandleStack does not do something. A tool's full entry, with an example call: get_docs page mcp/tools, section <tool name>. Show metrics in a table. The server's prompts walk through common tasks. On the web: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/; the resource candlestack://docs links them.

Starts a backtest of one of the user's models (with a manifest) on one instrument and period: it runs at once or waits in the user's queue (one runs at a time, 20 wait). It answers at once: follow it with wait_for_backtest, then get_backtest.

One backtest of a user runs at a time and up to 20 more wait in the queue, and a few run at once over all users, taking turns; a queued one answers its place and `eta_s`. The run takes from seconds to minutes.

Pass an `idempotency_key` (a UUID you make) to call it again safely after a timeout: the same call with the same key within 24 hours answers the first backtest instead of starting another. Read the engine and metrics pages before you explain a setting or a result.
